chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who struck another man’s ear with a bone, and he claimed that all of his hearing had gone. He said: “He is to be given a delay of one year, and he is to be watched by two just witnesses. If they come and testify that he heard and that he responded upon hearing, then he has no right. But if it is not discovered that he heard, he is made to swear an oath, then he is given the blood money.” He said: I said, “What if he hears after he has been given the blood money?” He said: “It is something Allah, the Exalted, has given him.”

He said: And I asked him about the eye, whose owner claims that he does not see with it. He said: “He is to be given a delay of one year, then after the year he is made to swear that he does not see, then he is given the blood money.” I said, “What if he sees after that?” He said: “It is something Allah has given him.”

key_terms.أُذُنَ رَجُلٍ: a man’s ear, the injured organ in the legal case
key_terms.بِشَاهِدَيْ عَدْلٍ: by two just witnesses, a standard of legal verification
key_terms.سَمْعُهُ كُلُّهُ: his hearing entirely, meaning total loss of hearing
key_terms.لَا يُبْصِرُ بِهَا: he does not see with it, meaning claimed loss of sight
key_terms.ٱسْتُحْلِفَ: he is made to swear an oath, as part of judicial procedure
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: blood money, the prescribed financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.ٱلْعَيْنِ: the eye, the second organ discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rule on blood money for claimed loss of hearing or sight after injury?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on claims of loss of hearing or sight due to injury. The claimant is given a one-year period, with verification through just witnesses in the case of hearing, and then an oath if the loss remains unproven by observation; after that, blood money is awarded. If the person later regains the faculty, the compensation is not reversed, as its return is treated as a gift granted by Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5290 - It is narrated from Ibn Mahbub from his father from Hammad ibn Ziyad from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who struck another man's ear with a bone, and the man claimed that he had completely lost his hearing.
Imam (as) said: "He should be given a respite for one year, and two just witnesses should observe him. If they testify that he heard and responded to hearing, then he has no right (to compensation).
But if it cannot be confirmed that he heard, he should be made to swear an oath, and then he should be given the full compensation (blood money)."
I asked: "What if he regains his hearing after receiving the compensation?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is something Allah (swt) the Exalted has granted him."

I then asked Imam (as) about someone who claimed he could no longer see with his eye.
Imam (as) said: "He should be given a respite for one year, and after the year, he should swear an oath that he cannot see, and then he should be given the full compensation (blood money)."
I asked: "What if he regains his sight after that?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is something Allah (swt) has granted him."
